description: Probability of a failed or inadequate office endometrial biopsy in Lynch syndrome surveillance populations
source: Simple pooled proportion across three Lynch-specific surveillance studies confirmed genuinely Pipelle-specific via direct primary-source full-text verification (2026-08-31, institutional access): Elmasry et al. 2009 (Fam Cancer 8:431-439, PMID 19526324) 5/25 -- Table 3's 'Pipelle done' column: 20 successful (all 'Normal' histology), 5 failures (3 atrophic endometrium, 1 cannulation failure from pain, 1 no-access from prior endometrial resection); Lecuru et al. 2008 (Int J Gynecol Cancer 18:1326-1331, PMID 18217965) 12/116 -- Methods state biopsy was performed with a 'Pipelle de Cornier device' for all attempts, Results report 12 (10%) failures; Woolderink et al. 2020 (BMC Womens Health 20:54, PMID 32183830, open access) 5/25 -- Table 2: 18 sufficient + 5 insufficient of 23 attempted, denominator 25 includes 2 women who never underwent sampling (cervical stenosis, fear of pain).
notes: Base value = pooled proportion (5+12+5)/(25+116+25) = 22/166 = 0.133 (was 0.137). CORRECTED 2026-08-31 after direct primary-source verification found two errors in the NIHR systematic review's Table 11 (NBK606812/table/table11), which this parameter previously relied on without independently reading the primary papers: (1) Elmasry's true Pipelle failure count is 5/25 (20.0%), not 6/25 (24.0%) as the review's table stated -- recounted twice from Table 3 to confirm; (2) Rijcken et al. 2003 (PMID 14529665) is NOT a Pipelle-specific study -- full-text Table 2 shows it used a mix of five sampling methods (Pipelle, VABRA, hysteroscopy, curettage, hysteroscopy+curettage), and the '2/17' failures the NIHR review attributed to 'Pipelle' were actually from hysteroscopy and hysteroscopy+curettage attempts; all 4 of this study's genuinely Pipelle-specific samples succeeded (0/4). Rijcken was dropped from the pool entirely rather than corrected to 0/4, since a 4-patient Pipelle-only subset within an unrelated mixed-method study is not a meaningful independent replicate. Low/high (0.103-0.20) span the three individual study rates (Lecuru lowest, Elmasry and Woolderink tied highest). Simple unweighted pooled estimate, not a formal random-effects meta-analysis. Per this project's meta-rule that a study-frame-changing audit finding requires independent confirmation: this correction was verified against the primary full text of all three retained studies (not merely re-derived from the same secondary review that produced the original error), and Rijcken's exclusion was independently confirmed via its own full text. See docs/data_sources.md for the complete verification chain.

description: Fraction of failed/inadequate office EMB attempts that proceed to operative D&C, versus e.g. a repeat office attempt
source: No study of standalone office EMB in Lynch syndrome reports a repeat-office-attempt-vs-D&C-escalation fraction directly; the four Lynch EMB-failure studies underlying emb_failure_lynch (Elmasry 2009, Lecuru 2008, Rijcken 2003, Woolderink 2020) are all confirmed hard-paywalled with no free full text found (checked 2026-08-30). Two real, converging (non-Lynch) supporting citations: (1) Nebgen DE et al. 2014 (PMC4389779), MD Anderson's combined colonoscopy+EMB Lynch surveillance protocol, states explicitly: 'If cervical stenosis or insufficient endometrial tissue was encountered, hysteroscopy and dilation and curettage were scheduled' -- every EMB failure automatically escalates to D&C, no repeat-office-attempt step. (2) Yi Y et al. 2018 (Gynecol Oncol 150:112-118, PubMed 29747864), a general (non-Lynch) postmenopausal-bleeding Medicare decision-tree model, Table 1: 'P (moving to D&C if 1st attempted Pipelle failed) = 0.95 (range 0.94-1)' -- i.e. only 5% (range 0-6%) of patients get a repeat Pipelle attempt, based on the study authors' own expert clinical estimation.
notes: PROVISIONAL. Base case conservatively assumes 100% of office EMB failures escalate to D&C. This remains a placeholder for the STANDALONE office-EMB population specifically: no accessible study reports a repeat-office-attempt-vs-D&C-escalation split for that population, and the four candidate Lynch EMB-failure studies are all paywalled (see source). Tiered C (general/adjacent evidence, not direct-population evidence): two independent, real, non-Lynch citations (Nebgen et al. 2014's protocol language; Yi et al. 2018's published 95% estimate) now converge closely around the 100% base-case assumption, meaningfully strengthening it beyond an unfounded default -- but neither is a direct measurement of standalone office EMB in a Lynch surveillance population, so the value is deliberately left at 100% rather than adjusted to match either external figure. Needs either the (currently inaccessible) primary Lynch EMB-failure studies or a study of standalone office EMB practice patterns specifically to advance further.

description: Scheduling/staffing coordination cost to align gynecology and colorectal/endoscopy services for a combined visit

Time: practitioner estimate (Tyler Muffly, MD, Denver Health), 2026-08-28.
notes: PROVISIONAL (time component only). Base value = 2 schedulers (GYN + colorectal) x 30 min each x $22.08/hr = 2 x 0.5hr x $22.08 = $22.08. The wage component is real and cited; the TIME component (30 min/scheduler) is a practitioner estimate reflecting real institutional workflow, not an independently published source -- still flagged provisional for that reason, but materially better-grounded than the prior $25 unfounded guess it replaced (which was coincidentally close). Low/high vary both factors together: low = 2 x 15min x (wage x0.85) = 2 x 0.25hr x $18.77 = $9.38; high = 2 x 45min x (wage x1.15) = 2 x 0.75hr x $25.39 = $38.09. See scheduler_hourly_wage_onet_2025 for the wage component kept separately citable.

source: Moawad NS et al. Cost-Effectiveness of Office Hysteroscopy for Abnormal Uterine Bleeding. JSLS 2014;18(3):e2014.00393 (PMID 25392671), Table 1
notes: External validation/benchmark value, not wired into the base-case engine. Sum of physician fee $1356 + anesthesia fee $1190 + hospital fee $2400 (billing-department charges, 2014 dollars). Paired with cost_hysteroscopy_office_moawad_2014; the study's own two-strategy comparison (office-first-with-OR-rescue vs. all-OR) found $1498 savings per patient (95% CI $1051-$1923), structurally the same office-vs-institutional argument this repository makes for EMB vs. D&C, but for hysteroscopy in a non-Lynch AUB population.
